text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Three companies on Monday signed agreements with the Health Ministry for a 15-year concession worth 7.5 billion ringgit to provide medical support services to the 123 government hospitals.
- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the Cabinet would look at the mechanism used to implement development projects to ensure its effectiveness.
- Sun Microsystems Inc, popularly known for its Internet product JAVA, will light up the way for other companies to operate in the country's Multimedia Super Corridor.
- Malaysia Mining Corp has indeed pulled out of the Bakun Hydroelectric Project in a recent meeting among shareholders of the soon-to-be-listed infrastructure project company, a source said.
- A self-supporting pension fund will eventually take over the government's annual pension burden now totalling 3 billion ringgit, Treasury Secretary-General Cliffor Herbert said.

- Telekom Malaysia Bhd chief executive Mohamed Said Mohd Ali said the company is considering taking up a stake in a broadcasting company but refused to confirm market talk that it is eyeing a 20 percent stake in Sistem Television Malaysia Bhd (TV3).
